claims: The Iran nuclear agreement is officially known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA).
The JCPOA was reached on July 14, 2015.
The JCPOA was reached between Iran, the P5+1, and the European Union.
The P5+1 consists of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council—China, France, Russia, U.K., U.S.—plus Germany.
Breakout time is the time needed to produce enough weapons-grade uranium for a single nuclear weapon.
Under the JCPOA, Iran agreed to constraints on its nuclear program to increase breakout time from two or three months to at least one year.
Under the JCPOA, Iran reduced its enriched uranium stockpile by 98%.
Under the JCPOA, Iran capped enrichment levels at 3.67%.
90% enrichment is required for weapons.
Under the JCPOA, active centrifuges were reduced by two-thirds.
Under the JCPOA, active centrifuges were capped at 6,104 for ten years.
Under the JCPOA, only older models of centrifuges were allowed.
Under the JCPOA, the Arak heavy-water reactor was redesigned to prevent it from producing weapons-grade plutonium.
Under the JCPOA, spent fuel from the Arak reactor was to be shipped out of the country.
Under the JCPOA, the IAEA was granted 24-hour surveillance of facilities.
Under the JCPOA, the IAEA was granted the ability to inspect suspicious sites.
Implementation Day was January 16, 2016.
The IAEA verified compliance by Iran on January 16, 2016.
Following IAEA verification on January 16, 2016, the U.S., EU, and UN lifted nuclear-related economic sanctions.
The lifting of nuclear-related economic sanctions allowed Iran to regain access to billions of dollars in frozen assets.
The lifting of nuclear-related economic sanctions allowed Iran to regain access to international oil markets.
The JCPOA took effect on January 16, 2016.
President Donald Trump withdrew the United States from the JCPOA in May 2018.
President Donald Trump called the JCPOA "defective at its core."
President Donald Trump reinstated sanctions under a "maximum pressure" campaign.
Following the U.S. withdrawal, Iran gradually stopped complying with the JCPOA restrictions in 2019.
In 2019, Iran increased uranium enrichment to 60%.
In 2019, Iran reduced IAEA access.
President Joe Biden expressed a willingness to return to the JCPOA if Iran returned to full compliance.
In April 2026, it was reported that Iran officially terminated the JCPOA after 10 years.
